edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to the owner state variable in the Owned constructor, making ownership caller-controlled.
The Owned constructor reads msg.sender to initialize ownership.
transferOwnership is gated by the onlyOwner modifier which checks msg.sender against owner.
acceptOwnership authorizes the transfer by comparing msg.sender with newOwner before using it.
The _newOwner parameter is written directly into the newOwner state variable.
acceptOwnership checks msg.sender against newOwner to authorize the ownership transfer.
acceptOwnership assigns newOwner into the owner state variable.
acceptOwnership resets newOwner to address(0) after the transfer.
msg.sender indexes the balances mapping in transfer, allowing a caller to move their own tokens.
msg.sender indexes the allowed mapping in approve, granting an arbitrary allowance.
msg.sender indexes the allowed mapping in transferFrom to deduct the spender allowance.
msg.sender indexes the allowed mapping in approveAndCall before the external call.
The to parameter indexes the balances mapping as the transfer recipient.
The tokens parameter is subtracted from balances[msg.sender] in transfer.
The from parameter indexes balances as the debited account in transferFrom.
The to parameter indexes balances as the credited account in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter reduces allowed[from][msg.sender] in transferFrom.
balanceOf returns balances[tokenOwner] to the caller.
The tokenOwner parameter keys the allowed mapping in allowance.
The spender parameter keys the allowed mapping in allowance.
The spender parameter is written as a key in the allowed mapping by approve.
The tokens parameter is stored as the allowance value in approve.
The spender parameter keys allowed[msg.sender] in approveAndCall.
The tokens argument is forwarded into the external receiveApproval call.
The caller-supplied data is forwarded into the external receiveApproval call.
The tokenAddress parameter selects the arbitrary contract targeted by the external ERC20 transfer call.
The tokens parameter is forwarded to the external ERC20 transfer call.
safeAdd computes c = a + b from the a parameter.
safeAdd computes c = a + b from the b parameter.
safeSub computes c = a - b from the a parameter.
safeSub computes c = a - b from the b parameter.
safeMul computes c = a * b from the a parameter.
safeMul computes c = a * b from the b parameter.
safeDiv computes c = a / b from the a parameter.
safeDiv computes c = a / b from the b parameter.
transfer calls safeSub to deduct the sender balance.
transfer calls safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
transferFrom calls safeSub to deduct balances[from] and the spender allowance.
transferFrom calls safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
totalSupply performs an unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] without SafeMath.
approveAndCall invokes receiveApproval on an attacker-supplied spender contract, enabling reentrancy.
transferAnyERC20Token calls transfer on a caller-supplied token contract address.
The external receiveApproval call can reenter approve or transferFrom and manipulate the allowed mapping.
The external receiveApproval call can reenter transfer or transferFrom and manipulate token balances.
The arbitrary external token contract call can reenter iDeal and disturb balance accounting.
The iDeal constructor sets _totalSupply to the fixed initial token supply.
The iDeal constructor assigns the entire supply to the hardcoded owner address in balances.
The iDeal constructor sets the symbol state variable.
The iDeal constructor sets the name state variable.
The iDeal constructor sets the decimals state variable.
